overall.summary: Every claim and every prose number reproduces and no direction is wrong; four drafted wordings overreach: the 0.9 mm threshold with its '88 patients' caveat, 'any other thallium result' for numbers that hold for a normal scan only, a jargon reference case that does not show the stated threshold, and chest pain type left out of the pathway's inputs in the lead.

findings.statement: For 88 of the 242 training patients it already acts below about 0.9 mm (same wording in drafted.blocks[1], drafted.annotations.ann_34[4], drafted.readdown.ann_34.hypothesis[0] and drafted.hypothesis_revisions.ann_34).
findings.check: C64 support_check; subgroup oldpeak < 0.9; probe oldpeak by resting ECG and by thallium result
findings.evidence: The 88 counts patients whose swept curve already moves by more than 0.05 log-odds below 0.9 mm (a counterfactual sweep), not patients with ST depression below 0.9 mm on whom the part acts: of the 132 training patients with ST depression below 0.9 mm the part acts on 23. The 0.9 mm is the median fold; across patients it runs 0.7 to 1.7 mm (p10 to p90). The typical man opens between 0.8 and 1.0 mm, with hypertrophy on the resting ECG only at about 1.8 mm, and with a reversible defect the part is already on at 0 mm (+0.053). The sentence reads as a statement about real patients and does not say how far the threshold moves.
